shots.say: Where does rain come from? Who fills up the clouds?
Drip, drop! The rain falls on the hills.
Hi! I'm Gizmo. Let's find out where rain comes from!
Gizmo Explains!
Welcome to my lab, weather fans!
Today we follow some water, all the way around!
After the rain, there is a puddle in the park.
Out comes the sun. It warms the water in the puddle.
The sun warms lakes, and the ocean too. Vapor rises from them!
What does the sun give the water? Heat, or snow?
Heat! The sun's heat makes the water cycle work.
Look! The puddle gets smaller, and smaller.
Where did the water go? Let's think!
The warm water turns into a gas. It is called water vapor.
Can we see water vapor? Yes, or no?
Water vapor is invisible! We drew it as little dots, so you can see it.
The vapor floats high into the sky.
Point up to the sky, where the vapor goes!
Where does the vapor go? Up to the sky, or under the ground?
Water turns into vapor. This is called evaporation!
Wiggle your fingers and float them up, like vapor!
Say it with me. The sun warms the water!
What does warm water turn into? Vapor, or sand?
Vapor! The sun warms the water, and the vapor floats up.
High up in the sky, the air is very cold.
The cold turns the vapor back into tiny drops of water.
Back into water? Let's look closer!
Each tiny drop forms on a tiny speck of dust, smoke, or salt.
What does a tiny drop form on? A speck of dust, or a shoe?
A speck of dust! So tiny, you can not see it.
Lots and lots of tiny drops make a cloud!
Vapor turns back into water. This is called condensation!
You can see this at home! On a cold winter day, look at a window.
Drops of water form on the inside of the glass!
Where do drops form at home on a cold day? On a window, or on a pillow?
Is condensation the same as evaporation, or the opposite?
The opposite! Water goes up as vapor, and comes back as drops.
Make a big round cloud with your arms!
Say it with me. Cold air makes clouds!
What is a cloud made of? Tiny drops of water, or cotton candy?
Tiny drops of water, high up in the cold sky!
Inside a cloud, the tiny drops bump together.
They join, and grow into bigger drops!
Big drops are heavy. What happens next? They fall, or float away?
They fall! Gravity pulls them down to the ground.
Down comes the rain! Pitter, patter!
When it is very cold, the drops can fall as snow.
What can fall from a very cold cloud? Snow, or leaves?
Snow! Soft, white snow comes from clouds too.
Tap your fingers on your legs, like falling rain!
The rain flows downhill, into a river.
Rivers carry the water to lakes, and to the ocean.
And look! The rain fills up the puddle in the park again.
Which way does rain water flow? Downhill, or uphill?
Then the sun warms the water again. Round and round it goes!
This is the water cycle. It is always happening, everywhere!
Let's count the steps. Warm, rise, cloud, rain!
Spin around slowly, like the water cycle!
Say it with me. Round and round goes the water!
Quiz time! Let's remember what we learned.
What warms the water in the puddle? The sun, or the moon?
The sun! The water floats up as vapor.
What makes a cloud? Tiny drops of water, or tiny rocks?
Tiny drops of water, in the cold air!
Why do drops fall as rain? They get heavy, or they get sleepy?
They get heavy! Down comes the rain.
Sun, vapor, cloud, rain! Thanks for exploring with me!
Gizmo Explains!
